newsitem.title: ITALY: UPS Spain workers plan strike action.
newsitem.headline: UPS Spain workers plan strike action.

text.p: Union members employed by United Parcel Service of America Inc (UPS) in Spain plan strike action to coincide with stoppages by Italian colleagues in protest against threatened job cuts, union sources said.
Union delegates from UPS Barcelona intend to hold a joint press conference with Italian unions in Milan on Wednesday.

Earlier, Italian UPS union sources said Italian staff will hold an eight hour strike on March 28 in protest against 150 job cuts, with some 85 percent of the 900 UPS staff in Italy expected to be involved in the stoppage.
Limited strike action is also planned by Milan-based staff on Wednesday as 82 of the job losses concern the company's Milan operation.
UPS Italy announced the redundancies on March 6 in order to "remain competitive and cost efficient in the Italian express distribution market."
Atlanta-based UPS is the world's largest package distribution company.
The Spanish union sources said UPS Spain had been carrying out a restructuring policy since 1992 in all its regional branches except Madrid, but so far the unions had managed to prevent any job cuts.
Unions and management were currently discussing an in-house contract which should be valid for the next two years.
The sources said union proposals were above all aimed at recovering the real value of salaries but the company was threatening to sack drivers in Barcelona and Madrid, a total of 140 people.

They said that management was also aiming to move 25 administrators from Madrid to its CTM centre which is the answering centre for the company's free phone number covering the whole of Spain. CTM operators have a separate, non UPS, contract.
The sources said UPS wanted to centralise this answering service in Brussels for the whole of Europe.
The Barcelona union representatives, who arrived in Milan on Monday, said UPS company policy was favouring international clients and causing a loss of national customers.
"The UPS password is to act like a millipede, if one leg breaks the others carry on," one union source said.

A spokesman for UPS in Milan said next Friday's national strike was likely to effect all its 25 operating points in Italy, the three airports where it has offices at Bergamo, Rome and Treviso as well as its Italian national warehouse in Milan and its international warehouse at Bergamo.
"At the moment I don't have details of measures we will take to guarantee a good service," the UPS spokesman said.
He said he could not comment on the situation in Spain.
